SMTO-PSM-0003 — That parameter name is already used by SMTO

GUID: 65e535a2-85e8-4a05-9d53-3e40f25f4105
Slug: parameter-reserved
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • The name you chose matches one of SMTO's built-in @ options, such as gateway, file or parameter, so the parameter wasn't saved under that name.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store, go to the Key field on the Overview tab, type a name that isn't a built-in @ option, for example my-gateway-login, and select Save. A parameter with a built-in name would clash with that option in the @ list, so SMTO won't allow it.
  2. Don't just change capital letters, spaces or dashes in the same name; add or change a word instead. SMTO ignores capitals and treats spaces and dashes as underscores, so "Check Terminal" still counts as the built-in check_terminal.
  3. Type @ in a message and check the parameter appears under its new name. This confirms you can now pick it from the @ list.

What success looks like

  • The parameter is saved and appears in the @ list under its new name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resubmitting the same name; it will always be refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter create or rename was rejected because the normalized key matches a reserved @ mention namespace, alias or special action ID.

What this means

  • Parameter creation or rename normalizes its key and finds it reserved for a built-in mention. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter creation or rename normalizes its key and finds it reserved for a built-in mention.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the intended canonical key with the reserved mention namespace before saving.

How to fix it

  • is_reserved() in agent_runtime/mentions compares the normalized key with MENTION_NAMESPACES IDs and aliases and SPECIAL_ACTIONS/MODE_ACTIONS IDs; both AgentParameterStore and MemoryParameterStore reject such keys on create and rename. Choose a key outside that set.
  • Rename this Parameter Store key to a nonreserved name, then select it from the @ palette.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A nonreserved unique key can be selected from the parameter palette.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
